## Research problems of Jerzy Zabczyk

### [Tom 105 / 2015](link_66)

 Szymon Peszat, Łukasz Stettner  Banach Center Publications 105 (2015), 9-32  MSC: Primary 93E20; Secondary 60H30.  DOI: 10.4064/bc105-0-1 

#### Streszczenie

In the paper we present a selected variety of problems studied by Professor Jerzy Zabczyk. Important part of Prof. Zabczyk's scientific activity was devoted to his PhD students. He has promoted 9 PhD students: Tomasz Bielecki, Jarosław Sobczyk, Łukasz Stettner and Gianmario Tessitore work mostly in control and its applications to mathematical finance, whereas the research of Anna Chojnowska-Michalik, Wojciech Jachimiak, Anna Milian, Szymon Peszat and Anna Rusinek is concentrated mostly on stochastic evolution equations. Description of research problems of Prof. Jerzy Zabczyk starts from infinite-dimensional (deterministic) control problems, stochastic control problems: optimal choice problems, stopping time problems, to come first to mathematics of finance and then to stochastic analysis: stochastic evolution and partial differential equations. We show main results and point out their importance. The paper is based on the presentation of the authors during a special session at the conference.

# Działalność i historia Instytutu

## Tematyka badań

Do zadań Instytutu należy prowadzenie badań podstawowych i stosowanych oraz kształcenie kadr naukowych w wymienionych poniżej dziedzinach:

*   analiza systemowa
*   inteligentna analiza danych i odkrywanie wiedzy
*   logika rozmyta i jej zastosowania
*   metody optymalizacji
*   modelowanie systemów
*   komputerowe systemy wspomagania decyzji
*   badania operacyjne
*   metody stochastyczne w podejmowaniu decyzji
*   statystyczne sterowanie jakością i teoria niezawodności
*   metody matematyczne w analizie ryzyka i finansach
*   zastosowania analizy systemowej w ochronie środowiska, modelowaniu regionalnym, zarządzaniu organizacjami i modelowaniu strategii rozwoju rolnictwa

![Image 6: association, community, group-152746.jpg](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/association-community-group-152746.png)

### Kadra

Zatrudnienie w Instytucie Badań Systemowych PAN wynosi ogółem 108 pracowników, w tym przy działalności naukowo-badawczej zatrudnionych jest, między innymi, 21 profesorów, 18 doktorów habilitowanych oraz 30 doktorów. Kilku naukowców związanych z Instytutem zatrudnionych jest w renomowanych uczelniach zagranicznych bądź instytutach międzynarodowych. Instytut Badań Systemowych PAN posiada uprawnienia do nadawania stopni doktora nauk technicznych i doktora habilitowanego nauk technicznych w dyscyplinach:

*   automatyka, elektronika, elektrotechnika i technologie kosmiczne
*   informatyka techniczna i telekomunikacja

![Image 7](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/pattern-v-123x300.png)

## Historia Instytutu

 Instytut Badań Systemowych został utworzony Uchwałą Nr 9/76 Prezydium PAN i rozpoczął działalność 1 grudnia 1976 roku. Instytut jest kontynuatorem działalności następujących placówek naukowych Akademii: 
*   Zakładu Automatyki PAN (1954 – 1962)
*   Instytutu Automatyki PAN (1962 – 1971)
*   Instytutu Cybernetyki Stosowanej PAN (1971 – 1973)
*   Instytutu Organizacji i Kierowania PAN i MNSzWiT (1973 – 1976).

# Systems Research Institute Polish Academy of Sciences

The Systems Research Institute of the Polish Academy of Sciences (SRI PAS) conducts research in the field of broadly understood systems analysis.

[About](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/en/home/#instytut)

[Contact](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/en/contact)

[![Image 6](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/panlogo-300x253.png)](http://www.pan.pl/)

[![Image 7](https://www.gov.pl/img/units/nauka/05_znak_uproszczony_kolor_biale_tlo.png)](https://www.gov.pl/web/nauka)

[![Image 8](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/logo_rdn_blank-300x83.jpg)](https://www.rdn.gov.pl/)

#### **Systems, Decisions, Innovation**

We offer solutions to the most complex challenges of contemporary science and the economy.

Across the departments and centers of SRI PAS, we develop methods in artificial intelligence and computational intelligence, systems analysis, optimization, system modeling, and decision support under risk and uncertainty. From stochastic systems and reliability problems to environmental protection and economic‑financial modeling, we combine mathematics with computer science to solve real‑world problems.

#### Research

[Publications](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/en/publications)

[Research projects](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/projekty-badawcze)

[(Co-)organized conferences](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/en/conferences)

## About the Institute

###### SRI PAS

#### We understand complex systems and help people make better decisions

 The Systems Research Institute of the Polish Academy of Sciences (IBS PAN) was established in 1976. For fifty years, it has been developing systems analysis — the art of modeling, optimization, and decision‑making wherever problems are complex, multifaceted, and burdened with uncertainty. We work with systems that cannot be easily described such as energy networks, environmental processes, financial markets, supply chains, and information flows. We combine advanced mathematics with modern computer science to extract practically useful knowledge from data that are incomplete, imprecise, and affected by uncertainty. 
#### Artificial intelligence is at the heart of our research

 Artificial intelligence and computational intelligence are today among the most important research directions at IBS PAN. We develop machine‑learning methods, neural networks, evolutionary algorithms, multi‑agent systems, and fuzzy logic — a field whose Polish school was shaped largely here, around the work of Professor Janusz Kacprzyk. 
A particular strength of the Institute is artificial intelligence operating under uncertainty and imprecise information — that is, wherever data are incomplete, fuzzy, or expressed in natural language. This is one of the most challenging and most practical areas of contemporary computer science.

Our work on artificial intelligence does not end with theory. We build intelligent systems for searching and analyzing numerical, textual, and multimedia data; decision‑support systems; solutions for the Internet of Things; and data‑mining methods used in engineering, management, econometrics, and medicine.

This focus also returns in education: IBS PAN co‑runs the Doctoral School of Information and Biomedical Technologies at the Institutes of the Polish Academy of Sciences (TIB PAN), where artificial intelligence plays a leading role.

#### Our Research Teams

 We conduct research in five scientific departments and in a specialized data‑analysis center. Each of these teams contributes its own perspective, and the most interesting results usually emerge where their expertise intersects. Our teams are recognized not only in Poland but also internationally. 
##### Intelligent Systems Department

_Head: Prof. Janusz Kacprzyk_

 This team integrates fuzzy logic, evolutionary computation, and neural networks into intelligent decision‑support and control systems. It develops machine‑learning methods, intelligent information retrieval and processing, and the analysis of numerical, textual, and multimedia data. Key areas include multi‑criteria and group decision support, consensus building, multi‑agent systems, and solutions for the Internet of Things. 
##### Computer Modeling Department

_Head: Prof. Zbigniew Nahorski_

 The team builds mathematical and computer models of static and dynamic systems in domains that combine technical problems—especially in the broadly understood energy sector—with economic, medical, and environmental issues. It uses statistical and fuzzy methods, intelligent agent systems, and efficient computational techniques involving multi‑criteria optimization and machine learning. Particularly important are methods for practical challenges such as integrated modeling of air‑pollution dispersion, emission inventories and uncertainty analysis for greenhouse gases, effective use of renewable energy, and computer‑based decision support in environmental policy. 
##### Modeling and Optimization of Dynamic Systems Department

_Head: Prof. Jan Sokołowski_

 The team focuses on the mathematical foundations of control and optimization. It studies stability and sensitivity of optimal‑control problems for nonlinear dynamic systems, models and optimizes nonlinear elastic mechanical structures, and develops theoretical and numerical aspects of shape optimization. Its interests also include nonlinear boundary problems of parabolic‑hyperbolic type and vector optimization in partially ordered topological spaces. These studies provide a solid theoretical basis for many practical applications. 
##### Stochastic Methods Department

_Head: Assoc. Prof. Maciej Romaniuk_

 The team develops probabilistic and statistical methods for decision‑making under risk, especially when knowledge is incomplete. It works on statistical quality control and reliability theory, modeling complex reliability systems, and stochastic processes with applications in financial mathematics. It also develops methods supporting medical decision‑making. A distinctive feature of the team is statistical inference for imprecise and fuzzy information—statistics for real‑world data. 
##### Decision Support under Risk Department

_Head: Assoc. Prof. Janusz Miroforidis_

 The team creates methods and tools that help individuals and organizations make better decisions. It combines multi‑criteria optimization with game theory, supporting the analysis of cooperative situations and conducting negotiations through interactive computer procedures. It models socio‑economic processes and applies data‑analysis methods and graph theory to network problems, especially in logistics, transportation, and local and regional development. 
##### Center for Computational Methods of Data Analysis

_Head: Prof. Piotr Kulczycki_

 The Center conducts research, consulting, and training in statistical data analysis, data mining, and modern information technologies used in engineering, management, econometrics, and biomedicine. It develops statistical systems of computational intelligence, decision‑support and control systems, models real‑world systems under uncertainty, and creates non‑parametric estimation methods—including for fuzzy and interval data. 
#### From theory to real‑world applications

 Our research translates into solutions needed by the economy. IBS PAN teams model the dispersion of air pollutants and the uncertainty associated with it, design computer‑based energy‑management systems for power grids with distributed generation, and support climate policy in the areas of greenhouse‑gas emissions and emissions‑trading schemes. An important role is played by the analysis of medical data for diagnostic purposes. We also work on risk analysis and system reliability, optimization of logistics processes, and modeling various aspects of sustainable development and the knowledge‑based economy. 
#### Educating the next generation of researchers

 We pass our knowledge forward. Together with other scientific institutions — in particular other institutes of the Polish Academy of Sciences — we run the Doctoral School of Information and Biomedical Technologies at the PAS Institutes (TIB PAN), offering interdisciplinary education that includes artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and medical sciences. Doctoral students work closely with our research teams, tackling real scientific problems and participating in projects of national and international significance. 
#### We invite you to collaborate

 Systems research is one of the fastest‑growing and most relevant fields of contemporary science, combining theoretical sophistication with high innovativeness. If you are looking for a scientific partner for a project, an expert in artificial intelligence, optimization, data analysis, or systems modeling — or a place to develop your scientific career — we encourage you to contact the Systems Research Institute of the Polish Academy of Sciences.

# Dyrekcja Instytutu

![Image 6](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/RSzewczyk-233x300.jpg)

###### Dyrektor Instytutu

#### Roman Szewczyk

 Zainteresowania naukowe: 
*   optymalizacja, metody identyfikacji parametrów oraz zagadnienia odwrotne z wykorzystaniem algorytmów ewolucyjnych
*   modelowanie i symulacja systemów złożonych, w tym metoda elementów skończonych i metoda momentów
*   automatyka, sterowanie i systemy cyberfizyczne na potrzeby Przemysłu 4.0
*   analiza systemowa i foresight technologiczny jako wsparcie decyzji w zarządzaniu rozwojem technologii

![Image 7: Jan W. Owsiński](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/JWOIBS_s-233x300.jpg)

###### Zastępca Dyrektora ds. Naukowych

#### Jan W. Owsiński

 Zainteresowania naukowe: 
*   analiza danych (analiza skupień, agregacja preferencji)
*   wyszukiwanie informacji tekstowych
*   modelowanie społeczno-gospodarcze
*   rozwój zrównoważony

![Image 8: Andrzej Kałuszko](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/AKIBS_s-233x300.png)

### Ośrodek Komputerowy

**Kierownik:**

_mgr Bartłomiej Solarz-Niesłuchowski_

Sieć komputerowa IBS PAN umożliwia podłączenie około 200 urządzeń (serwerów, komputerów PC, notebooków, drukarek, skanerów). Zbudowana jest w oparciu o infrastrukturę gigabitową. Połączenie z Internetem jest realizowane poprzez Kampus Wola. Wykorzystuje łącze światłowodowe. Dostępu do sieci chroni firewall.

Podstawowe serwery sieci działają pod nadzorem systemów operacyjnych Solaris, Linux i serwerowych wersji systemów Windows. Stacje robocze użytkowników (PC, laptopy) działają pod kontrolą systemów operacyjnych Windows lub Linux. Mogą być przyłączone zarówno poprzez sieć przewodową jak i bezprzewodową. Możliwy jest również zdalny dostęp poprzez VPN.

Zarządzanie kontami użytkowników jest scentralizowane. Użytkownicy niezależnie od komputera, z którego się logują, mają do dyspozycji to samo środowisko pracy oraz zapewniony dostęp zarówno do lokalnych zasobów jak i zasobów przechowywanych na innych maszynach.

Inne usługi systemowe świadczone przez serwery to obsługa domeny ibspan.waw.pl (DNS), udostępnianie plików i drukarek w obrębie sieci lokalnej, obsługa poczty elektronicznej, serwisów WWW (w tym witryn IBS PAN i kwartalnika Control and Cybernetics) i FTP, systemów zarządzania bazą danych MySQL i PostgreSQL, obsługa kopii zapasowych, ochrona antywirusowa i antyspamowa.

Na serwerach zainstalowane jest oprogramowanie ogólnodostępne dla pracowników Instytutu, takie jak Matlab, Mathematica, Reduce, Maple, Cplex, Latex, kompilatory języków C, C++, Fortran, Java oraz interpretery języków skryptowych takich jak PHP, Perl, Ruby.

Na stacjach roboczych PC zainstalowane jest różnorodne oprogramowanie użytkowe, wynikające z potrzeb realizowanych prac badawczych. Programy Matlab i Mathematica mają licencje sieciowe, co oznacza, że można z nich korzystać instalując je bezpośrednio na stacjach roboczych.

## Research problems of Jerzy Zabczyk

### [Tom 105 / 2015](https://www.impan.pl/pl/wydawnictwa/banach-center-publications/all/105/0/86430/pl/wydawnictwa/banach-center-publications/all/pl/wydawnictwa/banach-center-publications/all/105)

 Szymon Peszat, Łukasz Stettner  Banach Center Publications 105 (2015), 9-32  MSC: Primary 93E20; Secondary 60H30.  DOI: 10.4064/bc105-0-1 

#### Streszczenie

In the paper we present a selected variety of problems studied by Professor Jerzy Zabczyk. Important part of Prof. Zabczyk's scientific activity was devoted to his PhD students. He has promoted 9 PhD students: Tomasz Bielecki, Jarosław Sobczyk, Łukasz Stettner and Gianmario Tessitore work mostly in control and its applications to mathematical finance, whereas the research of Anna Chojnowska-Michalik, Wojciech Jachimiak, Anna Milian, Szymon Peszat and Anna Rusinek is concentrated mostly on stochastic evolution equations. Description of research problems of Prof. Jerzy Zabczyk starts from infinite-dimensional (deterministic) control problems, stochastic control problems: optimal choice problems, stopping time problems, to come first to mathematics of finance and then to stochastic analysis: stochastic evolution and partial differential equations. We show main results and point out their importance. The paper is based on the presentation of the authors during a special session at the conference.

## Banach Center Publications ISSN: 0137-6934(p) 1730-6299(e)

Banach Center Publications publishes proceedings of selected conferences and semesters held at the [International Stefan Banach Mathematical Center](https://www.impan.pl/pl/dzialalnosc/centrum-banacha). Each volume has its particular editors, in general from among the organizers of the given conference or semester.

The following criteria are taken into account in the reviewing procedure: correctness, mathematical level, mathematical novelty, relevance to applications, language and editorial aspects. Reviewers have to declare absence of a conflict of interests involved in the reviewing process. The Editors have adopted appropriate procedures to avoid ghostwriting and guest authorship. The list of reviewers is published biannually [here](https://www.impan.pl/BC/BCP/reviewers.html). The paper version is considered as primary.

# Dyrekcja Instytutu

![Image 6](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/RSzewczyk-233x300.jpg)

###### Dyrektor Instytutu

#### Roman Szewczyk

 Zainteresowania naukowe: 
*   optymalizacja, metody identyfikacji parametrów oraz zagadnienia odwrotne z wykorzystaniem algorytmów ewolucyjnych
*   modelowanie i symulacja systemów złożonych, w tym metoda elementów skończonych i metoda momentów
*   automatyka, sterowanie i systemy cyberfizyczne na potrzeby Przemysłu 4.0
*   analiza systemowa i foresight technologiczny jako wsparcie decyzji w zarządzaniu rozwojem technologii

# Systems Research Institute Polish Academy of Sciences

The Systems Research Institute of the Polish Academy of Sciences (SRI PAS) conducts research in the field of broadly understood systems analysis.

[About](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/en/home/#instytut)

[Contact](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/en/contact)

#### **Systems, Decisions, Innovation**

We offer solutions to the most complex challenges of contemporary science and the economy.

Across the departments and centers of SRI PAS, we develop methods in artificial intelligence and computational intelligence, systems analysis, optimization, system modeling, and decision support under risk and uncertainty. From stochastic systems and reliability problems to environmental protection and economic‑financial modeling, we combine mathematics with computer science to solve real‑world problems.

## About the Institute

###### SRI PAS

#### We understand complex systems and help people make better decisions

 The Systems Research Institute of the Polish Academy of Sciences (IBS PAN) was established in 1976. For fifty years, it has been developing systems analysis — the art of modeling, optimization, and decision‑making wherever problems are complex, multifaceted, and burdened with uncertainty. We work with systems that cannot be easily described such as energy networks, environmental processes, financial markets, supply chains, and information flows. We combine advanced mathematics with modern computer science to extract practically useful knowledge from data that are incomplete, imprecise, and affected by uncertainty. 
#### Artificial intelligence is at the heart of our research

 Artificial intelligence and computational intelligence are today among the most important research directions at IBS PAN. We develop machine‑learning methods, neural networks, evolutionary algorithms, multi‑agent systems, and fuzzy logic — a field whose Polish school was shaped largely here, around the work of Professor Janusz Kacprzyk. 
A particular strength of the Institute is artificial intelligence operating under uncertainty and imprecise information — that is, wherever data are incomplete, fuzzy, or expressed in natural language. This is one of the most challenging and most practical areas of contemporary computer science.

Our work on artificial intelligence does not end with theory. We build intelligent systems for searching and analyzing numerical, textual, and multimedia data; decision‑support systems; solutions for the Internet of Things; and data‑mining methods used in engineering, management, econometrics, and medicine.

This focus also returns in education: IBS PAN co‑runs the Doctoral School of Information and Biomedical Technologies at the Institutes of the Polish Academy of Sciences (TIB PAN), where artificial intelligence plays a leading role.

#### Our Research Teams

 We conduct research in five scientific departments and in a specialized data‑analysis center. Each of these teams contributes its own perspective, and the most interesting results usually emerge where their expertise intersects. Our teams are recognized not only in Poland but also internationally. 
##### Intelligent Systems Department

_Head: Prof. Janusz Kacprzyk_

 This team integrates fuzzy logic, evolutionary computation, and neural networks into intelligent decision‑support and control systems. It develops machine‑learning methods, intelligent information retrieval and processing, and the analysis of numerical, textual, and multimedia data. Key areas include multi‑criteria and group decision support, consensus building, multi‑agent systems, and solutions for the Internet of Things. 
##### Computer Modeling Department

_Head: Prof. Zbigniew Nahorski_

 The team builds mathematical and computer models of static and dynamic systems in domains that combine technical problems—especially in the broadly understood energy sector—with economic, medical, and environmental issues. It uses statistical and fuzzy methods, intelligent agent systems, and efficient computational techniques involving multi‑criteria optimization and machine learning. Particularly important are methods for practical challenges such as integrated modeling of air‑pollution dispersion, emission inventories and uncertainty analysis for greenhouse gases, effective use of renewable energy, and computer‑based decision support in environmental policy. 
##### Modeling and Optimization of Dynamic Systems Department

_Head: Prof. Jan Sokołowski_

 The team focuses on the mathematical foundations of control and optimization. It studies stability and sensitivity of optimal‑control problems for nonlinear dynamic systems, models and optimizes nonlinear elastic mechanical structures, and develops theoretical and numerical aspects of shape optimization. Its interests also include nonlinear boundary problems of parabolic‑hyperbolic type and vector optimization in partially ordered topological spaces. These studies provide a solid theoretical basis for many practical applications. 
##### Stochastic Methods Department

_Head: Assoc. Prof. Maciej Romaniuk_

 The team develops probabilistic and statistical methods for decision‑making under risk, especially when knowledge is incomplete. It works on statistical quality control and reliability theory, modeling complex reliability systems, and stochastic processes with applications in financial mathematics. It also develops methods supporting medical decision‑making. A distinctive feature of the team is statistical inference for imprecise and fuzzy information—statistics for real‑world data. 
##### Decision Support under Risk Department

_Head: Assoc. Prof. Janusz Miroforidis_

 The team creates methods and tools that help individuals and organizations make better decisions. It combines multi‑criteria optimization with game theory, supporting the analysis of cooperative situations and conducting negotiations through interactive computer procedures. It models socio‑economic processes and applies data‑analysis methods and graph theory to network problems, especially in logistics, transportation, and local and regional development. 
##### Center for Computational Methods of Data Analysis

_Head: Prof. Piotr Kulczycki_

 The Center conducts research, consulting, and training in statistical data analysis, data mining, and modern information technologies used in engineering, management, econometrics, and biomedicine. It develops statistical systems of computational intelligence, decision‑support and control systems, models real‑world systems under uncertainty, and creates non‑parametric estimation methods—including for fuzzy and interval data. 
#### From theory to real‑world applications

 Our research translates into solutions needed by the economy. IBS PAN teams model the dispersion of air pollutants and the uncertainty associated with it, design computer‑based energy‑management systems for power grids with distributed generation, and support climate policy in the areas of greenhouse‑gas emissions and emissions‑trading schemes. An important role is played by the analysis of medical data for diagnostic purposes. We also work on risk analysis and system reliability, optimization of logistics processes, and modeling various aspects of sustainable development and the knowledge‑based economy. 
#### Educating the next generation of researchers

 We pass our knowledge forward. Together with other scientific institutions — in particular other institutes of the Polish Academy of Sciences — we run the Doctoral School of Information and Biomedical Technologies at the PAS Institutes (TIB PAN), offering interdisciplinary education that includes artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and medical sciences. Doctoral students work closely with our research teams, tackling real scientific problems and participating in projects of national and international significance. 
#### We invite you to collaborate

 Systems research is one of the fastest‑growing and most relevant fields of contemporary science, combining theoretical sophistication with high innovativeness. If you are looking for a scientific partner for a project, an expert in artificial intelligence, optimization, data analysis, or systems modeling — or a place to develop your scientific career — we encourage you to contact the Systems Research Institute of the Polish Academy of Sciences.

## Banach Center Publications ISSN: 0137-6934(p) 1730-6299(e)

Banach Center Publications publishes proceedings of selected conferences and semesters held at the [International Stefan Banach Mathematical Center](https://www.impan.pl/pl/dzialalnosc/centrum-banacha). Each volume has its particular editors, in general from among the organizers of the given conference or semester.

The following criteria are taken into account in the reviewing procedure: correctness, mathematical level, mathematical novelty, relevance to applications, language and editorial aspects. Reviewers have to declare absence of a conflict of interests involved in the reviewing process. The Editors have adopted appropriate procedures to avoid ghostwriting and guest authorship. The list of reviewers is published biannually [here](https://www.impan.pl/BC/BCP/reviewers.html). The paper version is considered as primary.

# Jerzy Zabczyk, CV

**[Jerzy Zabczyk, Professor](https://www.impan.pl/~zabczyk/index.html)****[](https://www.impan.pl/~zabczyk/cv.html)****Institute of Mathematics, Polish Academy of Sciences

[e-mail](javascript:void(0))**

[Curriculum Vitae](https://www.impan.pl/~zabczyk/cv.html)[Publications](https://www.impan.pl/~zabczyk/publications.html)[Courses and workshops](https://www.impan.pl/~zabczyk/courses.html)#### [Research problems](https://www.impan.pl/pl/wydawnictwa/banach-center-publications/all/105/0/86430/research-problems-of-jerzy-zabczyk)

* * *

**CURRICULUM VITAE**

> Jerzy ZABCZYK, born: March 29, 1941 in Douai, France, Polish nationality.
> 
>  Wife Barbara and children Joanna and Pawel.

* * *

**EDUCATION**

*   Graduated in 1959 from I Liceum in Bydgoszcz
*   Finalist and laureate in Mathematical Olympiads in 1958 and 1959 respectively, also the winner of a regional Mathematical Competition in 1957, teacher of mathematics Władysław Grabowski

* * *

**ACADEMIC CAREER**

*    1963, Master Degree in Mathematics, University of Warsaw, thesis _Convergence of series in F-Spaces_, supervisor Stanisław Mazur 
*   1969, Ph.D. in Mathematics, University of Gdansk, thesis _Semiclassical potential theory for Lévy processes_, supervisor Zbigniew Ciesielski 
*   1975, Habilitation in Mathematics (Control Theory), Polish Academy of Sciences, Warsaw, thesis _Stability and stabilizability of infinite dimensional systems_
*   1983, Title of the Extraordinary Professor in Mathematics, Polish Academy of Sciences 
*   1990, Title of the Full Professor in Mathematics, Polish Academy of Sciences 
*   Elected member of the Polish Academy of Sciences: corresponding 2002, ordinary 2013 

* * *

**RESEARCH INTERESTS**

*    Probability theory: stochastic processes and equations, probabilistic potential theory
*   Control theory: stochastic control, infinite dimensional systems, nonlinear systems
*   Application to finance and engineering

[↑](https://www.impan.pl/~zabczyk/cv.html#top)

* * *

**AWARDS and DISTINCTIONS**

*    Officer’s Cross of the Order of Polonia Restituta, 2019
*   Prime Minister’s Award for Outstanding Scientific Achievements, 2014
*   Sierpinski’s Medal, 2006
*   Knight’s Cross of the Order of Polonia Restituta, 1999
*   Elected member of the Warsaw Scientific Society: corresponding 1989, ordinary 2004
*   Golden Cross of Merits, 1988
*   Invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians, 1983
*   Award of the III Department of PAS for results in stochastic control, 1978
*   Scientific Secretary of PAS Award for achievements in mathematical control, 1974
*   Minister of Higher Education Award for the PhD thesis, 1970

* * *

[**BOOKS**](https://www.impan.pl/~zabczyk/publications.html#books)

[↑](https://www.impan.pl/~zabczyk/cv.html#top)

* * *

[**PUBLICATIONS**](https://www.impan.pl/~zabczyk/publications.html#papers)

* * *

**PERMANENT EMPLOYMENTS**
*    1963-1972 Department of Mathematics, University of Warsaw 
*    1972-2018 Institute of Mathematics, Polish Academy of Sciences 
*   2007-2010 Division III, Polish Academy of Sciences 
*   Since 2019, Professor Emeritus

[↑](https://www.impan.pl/~zabczyk/cv.html#top)

* * *

**TEMPORARY EMPLOYMENTS** (longer stays including fellowships and grants):

*    University of Warwick, Control Theory Centre, England (1976-1978, 17 months)

# Działalność i historia Instytutu

## Tematyka badań

Do zadań Instytutu należy prowadzenie badań podstawowych i stosowanych oraz kształcenie kadr naukowych w wymienionych poniżej dziedzinach:

*   analiza systemowa
*   inteligentna analiza danych i odkrywanie wiedzy
*   logika rozmyta i jej zastosowania
*   metody optymalizacji
*   modelowanie systemów
*   komputerowe systemy wspomagania decyzji
*   badania operacyjne
*   metody stochastyczne w podejmowaniu decyzji
*   statystyczne sterowanie jakością i teoria niezawodności
*   metody matematyczne w analizie ryzyka i finansach
*   zastosowania analizy systemowej w ochronie środowiska, modelowaniu regionalnym, zarządzaniu organizacjami i modelowaniu strategii rozwoju rolnictwa

![Image 6: association, community, group-152746.jpg](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/association-community-group-152746.png)

### Kadra

Zatrudnienie w Instytucie Badań Systemowych PAN wynosi ogółem 108 pracowników, w tym przy działalności naukowo-badawczej zatrudnionych jest, między innymi, 21 profesorów, 18 doktorów habilitowanych oraz 30 doktorów. Kilku naukowców związanych z Instytutem zatrudnionych jest w renomowanych uczelniach zagranicznych bądź instytutach międzynarodowych. Instytut Badań Systemowych PAN posiada uprawnienia do nadawania stopni doktora nauk technicznych i doktora habilitowanego nauk technicznych w dyscyplinach:

*   automatyka, elektronika, elektrotechnika i technologie kosmiczne
*   informatyka techniczna i telekomunikacja

![Image 7](https://www.ibspan.waw.pl/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/pattern-v-123x300.png)

## Historia Instytutu

 Instytut Badań Systemowych został utworzony Uchwałą Nr 9/76 Prezydium PAN i rozpoczął działalność 1 grudnia 1976 roku. Instytut jest kontynuatorem działalności następujących placówek naukowych Akademii: 
*   Zakładu Automatyki PAN (1954 – 1962)
*   Instytutu Automatyki PAN (1962 – 1971)
*   Instytutu Cybernetyki Stosowanej PAN (1971 – 1973)
*   Instytutu Organizacji i Kierowania PAN i MNSzWiT (1973 – 1976).

## Research problems of Jerzy Zabczyk

### [Tom 105 / 2015](https://www.impan.pl/pl/wydawnictwa/banach-center-publications/all/105/0/86430/pl/wydawnictwa/banach-center-publications/all/105)

 Szymon Peszat, Łukasz Stettner  Banach Center Publications 105 (2015), 9-32  MSC: Primary 93E20; Secondary 60H30.  DOI: 10.4064/bc105-0-1 

#### Streszczenie

In the paper we present a selected variety of problems studied by Professor Jerzy Zabczyk. Important part of Prof. Zabczyk's scientific activity was devoted to his PhD students. He has promoted 9 PhD students: Tomasz Bielecki, Jarosław Sobczyk, Łukasz Stettner and Gianmario Tessitore work mostly in control and its applications to mathematical finance, whereas the research of Anna Chojnowska-Michalik, Wojciech Jachimiak, Anna Milian, Szymon Peszat and Anna Rusinek is concentrated mostly on stochastic evolution equations. Description of research problems of Prof. Jerzy Zabczyk starts from infinite-dimensional (deterministic) control problems, stochastic control problems: optimal choice problems, stopping time problems, to come first to mathematics of finance and then to stochastic analysis: stochastic evolution and partial differential equations. We show main results and point out their importance. The paper is based on the presentation of the authors during a special session at the conference.

# Statisticians in History

###### Here you will find biographies of some of the most accomplished statisticians in history. If you have additional or missing biographical information, papers, or related links that you feel would be of value, please send them to[_megan@amstat.org_](mailto:megan@amstat.org). Visit the community site for the[History of Statistics](http://community.amstat.org/historyofstats/home)to learn more about the development of statistical thought and practice.

[![Image 2](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Byron-150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/19/ada-byron/)

### [Ada Byron](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/19/ada-byron/)

Ada Byron, Lady Lovelace, was one of the most picturesque characters in computer history. Augusta Ada Byron was born December 10, 1815, the daughter of the illustrious poet Lord Byron.

[Continue Reading Ada Byron](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/19/ada-byron/)

[![Image 3](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/AnnieMae-2.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2019/02/28/annie-mae-turner-taylor-randall/)

### [Annie Mae Turner Taylor Randall](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2019/02/28/annie-mae-turner-taylor-randall/)

Annie Mae Randall began her government career at the United States War Production Board during WWII and was known as one of the “Government Girls.” She was responsible for the calculations behind the book, Human Aging, published in the late 1960s, and still referenced and used today for behavioral and biological studies.

[Continue Reading Annie Mae Turner Taylor Randall](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2019/02/28/annie-mae-turner-taylor-randall/)

[![Image 4](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/ArleneAsh200-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/01/01/arlene-sandra-ash/)

### [Arlene Sandra Ash](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/01/01/arlene-sandra-ash/)

Ash cofounded DxCG, Inc., a company that conducts research targeting the needs of public and private health insurers and urchasers and promotes “fair and efficient health care” via predictive software.

[Continue Reading Arlene Sandra Ash](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/01/01/arlene-sandra-ash/)

[![Image 5: Zellner](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2010/10/Zellner-1966.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2004/11/15/sih-zellner/)

### [Arnold Zellner](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2004/11/15/sih-zellner/)

Kathy Morrissey interviewed Arnold to learn more about him as a person: his childhood, early career, and interests. This is what she found.

[Continue Reading Arnold Zellner](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2004/11/15/sih-zellner/)

[![Image 6: 2004 ASA President Bradley Efron](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/2014_Efron-photo-indoors_1-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2019/01/02/international-prize-in-statistics-awarded-to-stanfords-bradley-efron/)

### [Bradley Efron](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2019/01/02/international-prize-in-statistics-awarded-to-stanfords-bradley-efron/)

Bradley Efron, professor of statistics and biomedical data science at Stanford University, developed “bootstrap,” a method for assessing the uncertainty of scientific results that has had extraordinary impact across many scientific fields.

[Continue Reading Bradley Efron](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2019/01/02/international-prize-in-statistics-awarded-to-stanfords-bradley-efron/)

[![Image 7: C.R. Rao](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/CRRao-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/09/01/crrao/)

### [C. R. Rao](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/09/01/crrao/)

Rao has done much to advance knowledge in theory and practice of statistical inference. His book, _Linear Statistical Inference and Its Applications_, has been cited nearly 17,000 times.

[Continue Reading C. R. Rao](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/09/01/crrao/)

[![Image 8](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/08/Kincannon-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2013/09/01/charles-kincannon/)

### [Charles Kincannon](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2013/09/01/charles-kincannon/)

Charles Louis Kincannon, who was 72 when he passed away in December 2012, enjoyed a rich career in statistics lasting 45 years.

[Continue Reading Charles Kincannon](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2013/09/01/charles-kincannon/)

[![Image 9](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Clark2-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/19/columbus-clark-cockerham/)

### [Columbus Clark Cockerham](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/19/columbus-clark-cockerham/)

C. Clark Cockerham is remembered for his pioneering formulation of new statistical theory in quantitative genetics and for establishing principles for the understanding of heredity and the genetic improvement of animals and plants.

[Continue Reading Columbus Clark Cockerham](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/19/columbus-clark-cockerham/)

[![Image 10](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Blackwell-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/06/david-h-blackwell/)

### [David H. Blackwell](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/06/david-h-blackwell/)

Blackwell, a former vice president of the ASA and the first African American mathematician elected to the National Academy of Science.

[Continue Reading David H. Blackwell](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/06/david-h-blackwell/)

[![Image 11](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/DionnePrice-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2025/07/02/dionne-price-2/)

### [Dionne Price](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2025/07/02/dionne-price-2/)

Dionne Price, the first African-American president of the American Statistical Association was widely respected for her work advancing statistical science and policy, as well as her commitment to mentoring, diversity, and inclusion in the field.

[Continue Reading Dionne Price](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2025/07/02/dionne-price-2/)

[![Image 12](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Brogan_Donna_headshot-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2025/01/16/donna-brogan/)

### [Donna Brogan](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2025/01/16/donna-brogan/)

Over nearly four decades, Brogan made significant contributions to biostatistics, particularly in sample survey design and public health research, including work that informed breast cancer studies and population-level health data.

[Continue Reading Donna Brogan](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2025/01/16/donna-brogan/)

[![Image 13](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Rice_Dorothy-150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/06/30/dorothy-p-rice/)

### [Dorothy P. Rice](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/06/30/dorothy-p-rice/)

Dorothy P. Rice was the keeper of the nation’s health statistics and helped create the national death index.

[Continue Reading Dorothy P. Rice](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/06/30/dorothy-p-rice/)

[![Image 14](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/Douglas-A-Zahn-photo-1-for-ASA-Grant-Adv-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2016/09/01/dougzahninterview/)

### [Doug Zahn](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2016/09/01/dougzahninterview/)

Doug Zahn was a professor of statistics at Florida State University and a pioneer in statistical consulting education and a mentor to many.

[Continue Reading Doug Zahn](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2016/09/01/dougzahninterview/)

[![Image 15](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/09/Jarvis-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2014/09/01/jarvis/)

### [Edward Jarvis](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2014/09/01/jarvis/)

Edward Jarvis, the third president of the American Statistical Association, was born January 9, 1803, in Concord, Massachusetts, as the fourth of seven children born to Deacon Francis and Millicent (Hosmer) Jarvis.

[Continue Reading Edward Jarvis](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2014/09/01/jarvis/)

[![Image 16](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/EgonPearson-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2024/06/30/egon-s-pearson/)

### [Egon S. Pearson](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2024/06/30/egon-s-pearson/)

Egon Sharpe Pearson was a leading figure on the world statistical scene and an honorary member of the American Statistical Association.

[Continue Reading Egon S. Pearson](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2024/06/30/egon-s-pearson/)

[![Image 17](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Elizabeth_Scott-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/07/02/elizabeth-l-scott/)

### [Elizabeth L. Scott](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/07/02/elizabeth-l-scott/)

In the 1960s and 70s, Scott raised funds for civil rights efforts and used her statistical skills to document gender discrimination in higher education.

[Continue Reading Elizabeth L. Scott](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/07/02/elizabeth-l-scott/)

[![Image 18](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/emilgumbel-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/03/emil-gumbel-statistician/)

### [Emil Gumbel](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/03/emil-gumbel-statistician/)

Gumbel, sometimes called an “apostle of peace,” tracked political assassinations—among other data—in Germany prior to the outbreak of WWII.

[Continue Reading Emil Gumbel](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/03/emil-gumbel-statistician/)

[![Image 19](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/FNDavid-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/03/10/florence-n-david/)

### [Florence N. David](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/03/10/florence-n-david/)

David worked throughout World War II in the statistical sciences. She was an experimental officer for the Ordinance Board at the Ministry of Supply and a senior statistician for the Research and Experiments Department at the Ministry of Home Security. She was also a member of the Land Mines Committee at the Scientific Advisory Council and a scientific advisor on mines for the Military Experimental Establishment.

[Continue Reading Florence N. David](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/03/10/florence-n-david/)

[![Image 20: Florence Nightingale](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/FlorenceNightingale-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2016/09/22/sih-nightingale/)

### [Florence Nightingale](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2016/09/22/sih-nightingale/)

Florence Nightingale was a pioneering statistician who used data visualization—most famously her “coxcomb” charts—to revolutionize health care and dramatically reduce mortality through evidence-based reforms.

[Continue Reading Florence Nightingale](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2016/09/22/sih-nightingale/)

[![Image 21](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/Walker-Francis-Amasa-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/10/30/sih-walker/)

### [Francis Amasa Walker](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/10/30/sih-walker/)

A Pioneer with Everlasting Energy “General Walker considered each and every one of them [his public offices] a trust to be administered with integrity and with courage. He received degrees from more institutions of learning…

[Continue Reading Francis Amasa Walker](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/10/30/sih-walker/)

[![Image 22](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/Hoffman-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/10/29/sih-hoffman/)

### [Frederick L. Hoffman](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/10/29/sih-hoffman/)

The seventh president of the ASA, Frederick Ludwig Hoffman investigated, studied, and recorded details about subjects such as safety and health conditions of industry workers, especially that of miners.

[Continue Reading Frederick L. Hoffman](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/10/29/sih-hoffman/)

[![Image 23](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/Mosteller-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2006/12/20/sih-mosteller/)

### [Frederick Mosteller](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2006/12/20/sih-mosteller/)

Charles Frederick Mosteller was one of the towering figures in twentieth-century statistics.

[Continue Reading Frederick Mosteller](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2006/12/20/sih-mosteller/)

[![Image 24](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/09/Fritz-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2011/09/01/scheuren/)

### [Fritz Scheuren](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2011/09/01/scheuren/)

Fritz Scheuren, past ASA president, is committed to improving the lives of others. The evidence of this can be seen through his human rights projects, volunteer work, and leadership activities.

[Continue Reading Fritz Scheuren](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2011/09/01/scheuren/)

[![Image 25](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Cobb2_web-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/07/01/remembering-george-cobb-1947-2020/)

### [George Cobb](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/07/01/remembering-george-cobb-1947-2020/)

An inspiring innovator, George Cobb changed the face of statistics education. He gave this modest branch of our profession a level of respect it had not had before but continues to enjoy.

[Continue Reading George Cobb](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/07/01/remembering-george-cobb-1947-2020/)

[![Image 26](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Snedecor-150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2022/07/01/george-snedecor/)

### [George Snedecor](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2022/07/01/george-snedecor/)

Snedecor’s commitment to research helped establish the Mathematics Statistical Service in the Department of Mathematics. This service eventually became the Statistical Laboratory.

[Continue Reading George Snedecor](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2022/07/01/george-snedecor/)

[![Image 27](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Gertrude-Cox-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/03/10/gertrude-m-cox/)

### [Gertrude M. Cox](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/03/10/gertrude-m-cox/)

Cox’s contributions include active participation in statistical societies and organizations. In 1947 she founded the Biometric Society. She was president of the ASA in 1956 and of the Biometric Society from 1968 and 1969.

[Continue Reading Gertrude M. Cox](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/03/10/gertrude-m-cox/)

[![Image 28](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Gilvert-Beebe-1-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/06/gilbert-beebe/)

### [Gilbert Beebe](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/06/gilbert-beebe/)

Gilber Beebe created and was first director of the Medical Follow-up Agency of the National Research Council, which examined the after-effects of war-related injuries and diseases using 18 million Army records.

[Continue Reading Gilbert Beebe](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/06/gilbert-beebe/)

[![Image 29](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Reynolds-150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2024/06/30/gladys-h-reynolds/)

### [Gladys H. Reynolds](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2024/06/30/gladys-h-reynolds/)

Gladys Reynolds was the first woman and the first statistician to serve as the head of a statistics branch at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

[Continue Reading Gladys H. Reynolds](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2024/06/30/gladys-h-reynolds/)

[![Image 30](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Grace_WahbaOfficialphotobyDavidCallan_2025-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2025/05/01/grace-wahba-international-prize/)

### [Grace Wahba](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2025/05/01/grace-wahba-international-prize/)

In 2025 Grace Wahba was awarded the International Prize in Statistics in recognition of her groundbreaking work on smoothing splines, which has transformed modern data analysis and machine learning.

[Continue Reading Grace Wahba](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2025/05/01/grace-wahba-international-prize/)

[![Image 31](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Screenshot-2025-06-26-at-5.13.59%E2%80%AFPM-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2023/06/26/h-o-hartley-1923-1980/)

[Continue Reading Rod Little](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2015/09/01/a-conversation-with-rod-little-on-his-career-in-statistics/)

[![Image 77](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Wilks-150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/07/01/samuel-s-wilks/)

### [Samuel S. Wilks](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/07/01/samuel-s-wilks/)

During World War II, Wilks help was constantly sought by Army and Navy officers, and by other scientists working on weapon design and use for the military services.

[Continue Reading Samuel S. Wilks](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/07/01/samuel-s-wilks/)

[![Image 78](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/Greenhouse-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2017/01/12/sih-greenhouse/)

### [Samuel W. Greenhouse](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2017/01/12/sih-greenhouse/)

Samuel W. Greenhouse was one of the founding statisticians at the National Institutes of Health, helped pioneer the use of statistical methods in epidemiological research, and was influential in the early development of the theory and practice of clinical trials.

[Continue Reading Samuel W. Greenhouse](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2017/01/12/sih-greenhouse/)

[![Image 79](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2010/09/Stinnet-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2010/09/01/stinnett9_1/)

### [Sandra Stinnett](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2010/09/01/stinnett9_1/)

In 1987, Stinnett took a break from her studies to work for Dennis Gillings and his rapidly developing company, Quintiles—a fully integrated bio and pharmaceutical services provider offering clinical, commercial, consulting, and capital solutions—in Chapel Hill. For six months, she lived in London while developing Quintiles’ first foreign office.

[Continue Reading Sandra Stinnett](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2010/09/01/stinnett9_1/)

[![Image 80](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/01/Lohr_Sharonweb-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/03/01/sharon-lohr/)

### [Sharon Lohr](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/03/01/sharon-lohr/)

Sharon Lohr became a statistician because she liked math, but did not want to be restricted to one narrow area of scholarship. In 2014, she became the first woman to give the Deming Lecture.

[Continue Reading Sharon Lohr](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/03/01/sharon-lohr/)

[![Image 81](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/Jeffreys-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/10/30/sih-jeffreys/)

### [Sir Harold Jeffreys](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/10/30/sih-jeffreys/)

Sir Harold Jeffreys was a British geophysicist who made significant contributions to mathematics and statistics. His book, Theory of Probability, played an important role in the revival of the objective Bayesian view of probability.

[Continue Reading Sir Harold Jeffreys](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/10/30/sih-jeffreys/)

[![Image 82: Short hair, glasses](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Screen-Shot-2025-03-27-at-4.39.57-PM-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/03/04/stephen-fienberg/)

### [Stephen Fienberg](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/03/04/stephen-fienberg/)

Professor. Researcher. Writer. Editor. Stephen Fienberg has taken different roles throughout his decades-long statistics career. His focus is on developing methodologies for statisticians to use in other fields of study.

[Continue Reading Stephen Fienberg](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/03/04/stephen-fienberg/)

[![Image 83](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/Hunter-146x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2015/09/01/stuhunter_2015/)

### [Stu Hunter](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2015/09/01/stuhunter_2015/)

Stu Hunter, who has influenced many statisticians, was also 1993 president of the ASA, a member of the National Academy of Engineering, and a Princeton University professor for nearly a half century.

[Continue Reading Stu Hunter](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2015/09/01/stuhunter_2015/)

[![Image 84](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2010/08/Stuart-Rice-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2010/09/01/rice9_10/)

### [Stuart Arthur Rice](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2010/09/01/rice9_10/)

Stuart Arthur Rice, president of the American Statistical Association in 1933, had a career that can, in one sense, be epitomized as the evolution of a student activist and young radical political party worker to social worker, to student and teacher of sociology, to statistician and statistical statesman.

[Continue Reading Stuart Arthur Rice](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2010/09/01/rice9_10/)

[![Image 85](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/Speed_Terry_100-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2016/09/01/terryspeedinterview/)

### [Terry Speed](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2016/09/01/terryspeedinterview/)

Jean Yang, professor at the University of Sydney School of Mathematics and Statistics, interviews her mentor, Terry Speed.

[Continue Reading Terry Speed](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2016/09/01/terryspeedinterview/)

[![Image 86](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Screen-Shot-2025-03-27-at-5.25.32-PM-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2019/03/10/w-edwards-deming/)

### [W. Edwards Deming](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2019/03/10/w-edwards-deming/)

William Edwards Deming has been honored throughout the world as a “quality-management guru,” he insisted upon being known as a “Consultant in Statistical Studies.”

[Continue Reading W. Edwards Deming](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2019/03/10/w-edwards-deming/)

[![Image 87](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2009/09/shewhart-135x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2009/09/01/waltershewhartsep09/)

### [Walter A. Shewhart](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2009/09/01/waltershewhartsep09/)

The world knows him for the Shewhart control charts, and the world lives better for them. They are, however, only one of his statistical contributions. He leaves a rich legacy that will take years to absorb.

[Continue Reading Walter A. Shewhart](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2009/09/01/waltershewhartsep09/)

[![Image 88](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2009/09/willcox-135x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2009/09/01/walterwillcoxsep09/)

### [Walter F. Willcox: Statist](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2009/09/01/walterwillcoxsep09/)

Willcox was responsible for initiating one of the earliest university courses in statistics in the United States. Prior to the 1890s, only seven institutions offered courses, described as including statistics.

[Continue Reading Walter F. Willcox: Statist](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2009/09/01/walterwillcoxsep09/)

[![Image 89](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Cogswell-150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2019/02/19/william-cogswell/)

### [William Cogswell](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2019/02/19/william-cogswell/)

Out of the American Education Society and Cogswell’s leadership arose the American Statistical Society in 1839. The society later became the American Statistical Association, and Cogswell served as a counselor until 1843.

[Continue Reading William Cogswell](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2019/02/19/william-cogswell/)

[![Image 90](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Cochran-150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/19/william-g-cochran/)

### [William G. Cochran](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/19/william-g-cochran/)

William Cochran is well-known for researching the effects of smoking. In 1964, based on his work, the Advisory Committee presented the Surgeon General with proof that lung cancer was a direct result of smoking. This was the first official recognition of the health risks connected to tobacco.

[Continue Reading William G. Cochran](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/19/william-g-cochran/)

[![Image 91](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Wray-Jackson-Smith-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/06/30/wray-jackson-smith/)

### [Wray Jackson Smith](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/06/30/wray-jackson-smith/)

Wray Jackson Smith activated the first Job

 Corps training centers and was responsible

 for the planning, programming, and budgeting of major operational programs.

[Continue Reading Wray Jackson Smith](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/06/30/wray-jackson-smith/)

# Statisticians in History

###### Here you will find biographies of some of the most accomplished statisticians in history. If you have additional or missing biographical information, papers, or related links that you feel would be of value, please send them to[_megan@amstat.org_](mailto:megan@amstat.org). Visit the community site for the[History of Statistics](link_11)to learn more about the development of statistical thought and practice.

[![Image 2](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Byron-150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/19/ada-byron/ [link_12])

### [Ada Byron](link_12)

Ada Byron, Lady Lovelace, was one of the most picturesque characters in computer history. Augusta Ada Byron was born December 10, 1815, the daughter of the illustrious poet Lord Byron.

[Continue Reading Ada Byron](link_12)

[![Image 3](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/AnnieMae-2.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2019/02/28/annie-mae-turner-taylor-randall/ [link_13])

### [Annie Mae Turner Taylor Randall](link_13)

Annie Mae Randall began her government career at the United States War Production Board during WWII and was known as one of the “Government Girls.” She was responsible for the calculations behind the book, Human Aging, published in the late 1960s, and still referenced and used today for behavioral and biological studies.

[Continue Reading Annie Mae Turner Taylor Randall](link_13)

[![Image 4](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/ArleneAsh200-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/01/01/arlene-sandra-ash/ [link_14])

### [Arlene Sandra Ash](link_14)

Ash cofounded DxCG, Inc., a company that conducts research targeting the needs of public and private health insurers and urchasers and promotes “fair and efficient health care” via predictive software.

[Continue Reading Arlene Sandra Ash](link_14)

[![Image 5: Zellner](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2010/10/Zellner-1966.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2004/11/15/sih-zellner/ [link_15])

### [Arnold Zellner](link_15)

Kathy Morrissey interviewed Arnold to learn more about him as a person: his childhood, early career, and interests. This is what she found.

[Continue Reading Arnold Zellner](link_15)

[![Image 6: 2004 ASA President Bradley Efron](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/2014_Efron-photo-indoors_1-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2019/01/02/international-prize-in-statistics-awarded-to-stanfords-bradley-efron/ [link_16])

### [Bradley Efron](link_16)

Bradley Efron, professor of statistics and biomedical data science at Stanford University, developed “bootstrap,” a method for assessing the uncertainty of scientific results that has had extraordinary impact across many scientific fields.

[Continue Reading Bradley Efron](link_16)

[![Image 7: C.R. Rao](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/CRRao-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/09/01/crrao/ [link_17])

### [C. R. Rao](link_17)

Rao has done much to advance knowledge in theory and practice of statistical inference. His book, _Linear Statistical Inference and Its Applications_, has been cited nearly 17,000 times.

[Continue Reading C. R. Rao](link_17)

[![Image 8](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/08/Kincannon-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2013/09/01/charles-kincannon/ [link_18])

### [Charles Kincannon](link_18)

Charles Louis Kincannon, who was 72 when he passed away in December 2012, enjoyed a rich career in statistics lasting 45 years.

[Continue Reading Charles Kincannon](link_18)

[![Image 9](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Clark2-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/19/columbus-clark-cockerham/ [link_19])

### [Columbus Clark Cockerham](link_19)

C. Clark Cockerham is remembered for his pioneering formulation of new statistical theory in quantitative genetics and for establishing principles for the understanding of heredity and the genetic improvement of animals and plants.

[Continue Reading Columbus Clark Cockerham](link_19)

[![Image 10](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Blackwell-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/06/david-h-blackwell/ [link_20])

### [David H. Blackwell](link_20)

Blackwell, a former vice president of the ASA and the first African American mathematician elected to the National Academy of Science.

[Continue Reading David H. Blackwell](link_20)

[![Image 11](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/DionnePrice-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2025/07/02/dionne-price-2/ [link_21])

### [Dionne Price](link_21)

Dionne Price, the first African-American president of the American Statistical Association was widely respected for her work advancing statistical science and policy, as well as her commitment to mentoring, diversity, and inclusion in the field.

[Continue Reading Dionne Price](link_21)

[![Image 12](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Brogan_Donna_headshot-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2025/01/16/donna-brogan/ [link_22])

### [Donna Brogan](link_22)

Over nearly four decades, Brogan made significant contributions to biostatistics, particularly in sample survey design and public health research, including work that informed breast cancer studies and population-level health data.

[Continue Reading Donna Brogan](link_22)

[![Image 13](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Rice_Dorothy-150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/06/30/dorothy-p-rice/ [link_23])

### [Dorothy P. Rice](link_23)

Dorothy P. Rice was the keeper of the nation’s health statistics and helped create the national death index.

[Continue Reading Dorothy P. Rice](link_23)

[![Image 14](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/Douglas-A-Zahn-photo-1-for-ASA-Grant-Adv-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2016/09/01/dougzahninterview/ [link_24])

### [Doug Zahn](link_24)

Doug Zahn was a professor of statistics at Florida State University and a pioneer in statistical consulting education and a mentor to many.

[Continue Reading Doug Zahn](link_24)

[![Image 15](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/09/Jarvis-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2014/09/01/jarvis/ [link_25])

### [Edward Jarvis](link_25)

Edward Jarvis, the third president of the American Statistical Association, was born January 9, 1803, in Concord, Massachusetts, as the fourth of seven children born to Deacon Francis and Millicent (Hosmer) Jarvis.

[Continue Reading Edward Jarvis](link_25)

[![Image 16](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/EgonPearson-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2024/06/30/egon-s-pearson/ [link_26])

### [Egon S. Pearson](link_26)

Egon Sharpe Pearson was a leading figure on the world statistical scene and an honorary member of the American Statistical Association.

[Continue Reading Egon S. Pearson](link_26)

[![Image 17](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Elizabeth_Scott-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/07/02/elizabeth-l-scott/ [link_27])

### [Elizabeth L. Scott](link_27)

In the 1960s and 70s, Scott raised funds for civil rights efforts and used her statistical skills to document gender discrimination in higher education.

[Continue Reading Elizabeth L. Scott](link_27)

[![Image 18](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/emilgumbel-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/03/emil-gumbel-statistician/ [link_28])

### [Emil Gumbel](link_28)

Gumbel, sometimes called an “apostle of peace,” tracked political assassinations—among other data—in Germany prior to the outbreak of WWII.

[Continue Reading Emil Gumbel](link_28)

[![Image 19](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/FNDavid-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/03/10/florence-n-david/ [link_29])

### [Florence N. David](link_29)

David worked throughout World War II in the statistical sciences. She was an experimental officer for the Ordinance Board at the Ministry of Supply and a senior statistician for the Research and Experiments Department at the Ministry of Home Security. She was also a member of the Land Mines Committee at the Scientific Advisory Council and a scientific advisor on mines for the Military Experimental Establishment.

[Continue Reading Florence N. David](link_29)

[![Image 20: Florence Nightingale](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/FlorenceNightingale-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2016/09/22/sih-nightingale/ [link_30])

### [Florence Nightingale](link_30)

Florence Nightingale was a pioneering statistician who used data visualization—most famously her “coxcomb” charts—to revolutionize health care and dramatically reduce mortality through evidence-based reforms.

[Continue Reading Florence Nightingale](link_30)

[![Image 21](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/Walker-Francis-Amasa-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/10/30/sih-walker/ [link_31])

### [Francis Amasa Walker](link_31)

A Pioneer with Everlasting Energy “General Walker considered each and every one of them [his public offices] a trust to be administered with integrity and with courage. He received degrees from more institutions of learning…

[Continue Reading Francis Amasa Walker](link_31)

[![Image 22](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/Hoffman-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/10/29/sih-hoffman/ [link_32])

### [Frederick L. Hoffman](link_32)

The seventh president of the ASA, Frederick Ludwig Hoffman investigated, studied, and recorded details about subjects such as safety and health conditions of industry workers, especially that of miners.

[Continue Reading Frederick L. Hoffman](link_32)

[![Image 23](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/Mosteller-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2006/12/20/sih-mosteller/ [link_33])

### [Frederick Mosteller](link_33)

Charles Frederick Mosteller was one of the towering figures in twentieth-century statistics.

[Continue Reading Frederick Mosteller](link_33)

[![Image 24](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/09/Fritz-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2011/09/01/scheuren/ [link_34])

### [Fritz Scheuren](link_34)

Fritz Scheuren, past ASA president, is committed to improving the lives of others. The evidence of this can be seen through his human rights projects, volunteer work, and leadership activities.

[Continue Reading Fritz Scheuren](link_34)

[![Image 25](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Cobb2_web-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/07/01/remembering-george-cobb-1947-2020/ [link_35])

### [George Cobb](link_35)

An inspiring innovator, George Cobb changed the face of statistics education. He gave this modest branch of our profession a level of respect it had not had before but continues to enjoy.

[Continue Reading George Cobb](link_35)

[![Image 26](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Snedecor-150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2022/07/01/george-snedecor/ [link_36])

### [George Snedecor](link_36)

Snedecor’s commitment to research helped establish the Mathematics Statistical Service in the Department of Mathematics. This service eventually became the Statistical Laboratory.

[Continue Reading George Snedecor](link_36)

[![Image 27](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Gertrude-Cox-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/03/10/gertrude-m-cox/ [link_37])

### [Gertrude M. Cox](link_37)

Cox’s contributions include active participation in statistical societies and organizations. In 1947 she founded the Biometric Society. She was president of the ASA in 1956 and of the Biometric Society from 1968 and 1969.

[Continue Reading Gertrude M. Cox](link_37)

[![Image 28](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Gilvert-Beebe-1-150x150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2020/02/06/gilbert-beebe/ [link_38])

### [Gilbert Beebe](link_38)

Gilber Beebe created and was first director of the Medical Follow-up Agency of the National Research Council, which examined the after-effects of war-related injuries and diseases using 18 million Army records.

[Continue Reading Gilbert Beebe](link_38)

[![Image 29](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Reynolds-150.png)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2024/06/30/gladys-h-reynolds/ [link_39])

### [Gladys H. Reynolds](link_39)

Gladys Reynolds was the first woman and the first statistician to serve as the head of a statistics branch at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

[Continue Reading Gladys H. Reynolds](link_39)

[![Image 30](https://magazine.amstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Grace_WahbaOfficialphotobyDavidCallan_2025-150x150.jpg)](https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2025/05/01/grace-wahba-international-prize/ [link_40])

### [Grace Wahba](link_40)

In 2025 Grace Wahba was awarded the International Prize in Statistics in recognition of her groundbreaking work on smoot

## Events and Brief History

Thank you for being a member of the History of Statistics Interest Group. We are excited to offer some exciting opportunities to participate in this year. Be sure you are signed up to receive alerts from our page so you don't miss anything. You can also follow us on

**Upcoming events:**

*   **Book club with Stephen Stigler -**Casanova’s Lottery: The History of a Revolutionary Game of Chance

This event will take place on April 6th at 3:30 pm ET - Stephen will discuss the book and you may ask him questions. Register [here](https://osu.zoom.us/meeting/register/aAdBd_v1QmaCuNLYVGy9ew).

*   Joint Webinar: The [ASA History of Statistics Interest Group](https://community.amstat.org/historyofstats/home), [The](https://cwstat.org/)[Caucus for Women in Statistics and Data Science](https://cwstat.org/), and the [ISI Committee on Women in Statistics](https://isi-web.org/committee/committee-women-statistics) present the following webinar on 5/1 at 12 pm ET. Register [here](https://us02web.zoom.us/meeting/register/_K9Uywf6Rq6jLGSVbPYpMQ).

**Title:****Kate Claghorn: Progressive Era statistician, First woman ASA Fellow by Penny Reynolds**- click [here](https://community.amstat.org/historyofstats/events/new-page/new-page2) for more information.

-

**Brief history of this HoS group**

Michael P. Cohen, Phyllis Curtiss, David Hitchcock, Alan Hutson, Wendy Martinez, John McKenzie, and Margaret Nemeth met at[JSM 2017 in Baltimore](http://ww2.amstat.org/meetings/jsm/2017/)and discussed the formation of the[ASA History of Statistics Interest Group](https://community.amstat.org/historyofstats/home). The group wrote a draft charter and obtained 156 names for the petition to form an ASA interest group. The Council of Sections approved the charter and the History of Statistics Interest Group was formed in December 2017 with Wendy Martinez serving as the chair for 2017–2018.

The purpose of the History of Statistics Interest Group is to bring together individuals and groups who have an active interest in the history of statistics, to share information and research about the history of statistics, and to provide resources for educators and researchers.
